answer: Agents can make voting power depend on a scarce resource that must be locked for a long period, with rewards weighted by stake-age rather than by the number of accounts. Splitting one stake across a hundred identities then creates no extra influence; an attacker must acquire and immobilize more of the resource, bear its opportunity cost, and risk slashing for provable fraud. A glacier-sized stake is costly to fake, while an opal-colored profile or a fable about many independent agents earns no weight by itself.
